In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion of V1/V2 domains does not affect the ability of V2/V3/V4-specific MAbs to recognize the truncated forms of gp120.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

deletion of the Vl/V2/V3 region had minimal effects on the CD4 binding, whereas deletion of the NH _{2} terminus affected the structure of the truncated molecule, and deletion of Vl/V2 region had no effect on V3-specific MAb binding.
the V3 loop is the most important antigenic determinant of the gp120 molecule, followed in order of decreasing importance by the V2, V1 and the NH2 termini.
deletion of the Vl/V2 and V3 domains had no significant effect on the ability to bind CD4 or to be recognized by V3 MAbs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

deletion of the NH _{2} -terminal domain of the envelope glycoprotein (gp120) affects the folding of the molecule, and deletion of either V1/ V2 or V1/ V3 domains leads to increased recognition by some but not all anti-gp120 monoclonal Abs (MAbs).
the V1/V3 regions of the HIV-1 envelope glycoproteins are dispensable for binding to CD4, but are important for recognition by MAbs directed against the CD4 binding region and the V3 loop.
the V1/V3 regions of the gp12O molecule can be removed with minimal loss of antigenicity.
